page.layout: One column of centred text: an ornamental border, then the title EPIGRAMMA, a subtitle line, a verse epigram of six lines, and the initials B.C.P. below. No margin notes, running head or page number.

main_text.head: EPIGRAMMA
In Sixtum, aliâs Sextum, Quintum.
main_text.p: Omnia conuerso declinant ordine Romæ, Quod verè signum est, Roma, tui interitus. Adnumerare solent Papæ, (crescentis imago Imperii quod erat) sed modo dinumerant: Dinumera subito, Sixte, atque imponito finem, Vt sis ex numero, qui fueras numerus.

page.notes: The faint marks at the top right corner (a small figure, possibly "33") look like a handwritten or stamped number, not printed text, so they are left out. The ornamental border is a printer's decoration and is not transcribed. The six verse lines are run together in one paragraph because the schema has no line-break element for verse; the printed line breaks are as follows: lines 1 to 6 as in the paragraph above. The printed accent on "verè" is copied as shown.
